Here \(\bar{x} = 25\) and \(\sigma = 5\).

\(C.V. = 100 \times \frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}} = 100 \times \frac{5}{25} = 20\)

\(\therefore\) the coefficient of variation is \(20\%\)

Here \(\bar{x} = 150.4\) cm and \(C.V. = 2.5\).

Since \(C.V. = 100 \times \frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}}\), we get \(\sigma = \frac{C.V. \times \bar{x}}{100} = \frac{2.5 \times 150.4}{100} = \frac{376}{100} = 3.76\).

(The number of students, 65, is not needed — the coefficient of variation already links \(\sigma\) to \(\bar{x}\).)

\(\therefore\) the standard deviation of their heights is \(3.76\) cm
_note: The stem prints "coefficient of variance 2.5%", but the chapter defines only the Coefficient of Variation, C.V. = 100σ/x̄ — solved as C.V. The stem also reads "have their average height is 150.4 cm" (a stray "is"). Answer 3.76 matches the book's printed key.

solution:
For worker P: \(\bar{x}_P = 33,\ \sigma_P = 9\), so \((C.V.)_P = 100 \times \frac{9}{33} = \frac{900}{33} \approx 27.27\).

For worker Q: \(\bar{x}_Q = 21,\ \sigma_Q = 7\), so \((C.V.)_Q = 100 \times \frac{7}{21} = \frac{700}{21} \approx 33.33\).

The smaller coefficient of variation means the more consistent (less variable) performance, and \(27.27 < 33.33\).

\(\therefore\) worker P is more consistent

Speed is judged by the average time taken, not by the coefficient of variation: the worker with the smaller mean time finishes the job faster.

Mean time of P \(= 33\) hours, mean time of Q \(= 21\) hours, and \(21 < 33\).

\(\therefore\) worker Q seems to be faster in completing the job

The weekly wage bill of a department is (number of employees) \(\times\) (average weekly wage), i.e. \(n\bar{x}\).

First department: \(42 \times 750 = \text{Rs. } 31500\).

Second department: \(60 \times 400 = \text{Rs. } 24000\).

Since \(31500 > 24000\),

\(\therefore\) the first department has the larger wage bill

The means differ widely, so variability is compared by the coefficient of variation.

First department: \((C.V.)_1 = 100 \times \frac{8}{750} \approx 1.07\).

Second department: \((C.V.)_2 = 100 \times \frac{10}{400} = 2.5\).

Since \(2.5 > 1.07\),

\(\therefore\) the second department has larger variability in wages

solution:
The two subjects have different means, so compare by coefficient of variation.

Mathematics: \((C.V.)_M = 100 \times \frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}} = 100 \times \frac{2}{20} = 10\).

Statistics: \((C.V.)_S = 100 \times \frac{3}{25} = 12\).

Since \(12 > 10\),

\(\therefore (C.V.)_M = 10,\ (C.V.)_S = 12\) and Statistics shows the higher variability in marks
